historical_references.reference: Thayyib ibn Ziyad al-Qurashi was a prominent companion and close friend of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and was one of the Ten Promised Paradise. He was also a leading figure in early Islamic politics and administration. Thayyib was born in Mecca before the migration to Medina and was a member of the influential Qurashi tribe. He embraced Islam at an early age and was known for his piety, generosity, and courage. He played a significant role in the early Islamic community, particularly during the Caliphate of Abu Bakr (r. 632-634 CE). Thayyib participated in several military campaigns and was appointed as the governor of Kufa, an important city in Iraq, by Umar ibn al-Khattab (r. 634-644 CE). He is revered for his contributions to the spread of Islam and his unwavering dedication to the cause.

Another historical reference for Thayyib ibn Ziyad is his role as a mediator during the Ridda Wars. The Ridda Wars were a series of military campaigns launched by the early Islamic community to suppress rebellions by tribes who had renounced Islam after the death of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). Thayyib played a crucial role in negotiating peace treaties with several tribes in central Arabia, including the Banu Hanifah, Banu Bakr, and Banu Asad. His diplomatic skills and ability to negotiate effectively helped to establish peace and stability in the region during a critical period in Islamic history.
